desc: The shared vocabularies: reference kinds, events, vote thresholds, motion classes, temporal anchors. One namespace: references are kind/id (e.g. motion/amend, guard/no-question-pending, state/tabled, event/stated, queue/general-orders-current, class/bylaws, order/<id>, timer/table-expiry, table/appeal-yield-matrix). Kinds are closed naming law.

reference_kinds.table: named decision tables (precedence.json, voting.json, rules.json, scheduler.json)
reference_kinds.order: rules.json order objects (adopted debate-limiting orders etc.)
reference_kinds.question: lifecycle question object instances (runtime)

events.desc: One event vocabulary. 'origin' names the part that emits it. Core events are usable everywhere; prefer reuse over coining.

core.desc: a vote is being retaken by another (or a counted) method — division, retake-by-other-method motion, or chair's own retake

lifecycle.desc: committee reports the referred question back
a postponed question's set time reached (via scheduler)
unfinished business reached in the order of business

thresholds.desc: Canonical vote-threshold vocabulary. A motion's vote field lists sufficient alternatives — any one suffices. Compound forms combine previous notice with a threshold.

values.desc: more than half of votes cast
at least two thirds of votes cast
sustained by two thirds voting in the negative (e.g. objection-to-consideration: 'shall the question be considered')
chair's ruling stands unless a majority votes in the negative (appeal)
majority of all registered voting members (convention contexts)
effective on the demand of one member; no vote taken
decided by the chair's ruling, not a vote (appealable where applicable)
no question is put at all; the chair responds or acts (inquiries, requests answered directly)

motion_classes.B: bring-back (motions that bring a question again before the assembly)
motion_classes.M/B: main motion of the bring-back kind

temporal_anchors.desc: Timers reference these named anchors, never raw durations.
